acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Djinn family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Wisp-spirit, T1, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Half-Face Feint Initiate (Initiate) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two earth construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Small mostly vapor Wisp-spirit with only a half-formed face, faint warm glow, no jewelry, and no defined torso.
Signature mechanic: Unfinished Glance: the half-face forms on one side of the vapor and darts along that gaze before dissolving.
battlefieldDuty: Probe target reading with one vapor feint that resolves only when the half-face turns complete.
constructionDimensions: Material/structure branches: T1 vapor, half-face, and trailing plume gain a mineral boundary clamp; T2 the defined torso and plain cuffs gain crystal load keys; T3 visible wind arms and orbiting rings gain sediment weights; T4 crown and sacred script gain fractured anchor glyphs; T5 vortex, throne, and lamps gain bounded throne braces.

Motion/process branches: T1 the vapor half-face briefly loads the plume clamp while hovering; T2 the torso transfers weight through one cuff key; T3 the wind arms alternate orbiting-ring loads; T4 crown script commits one anchor glyph; T5 vortex, throne, and lamps load and release one throne brace.
counterplay: Cross behind the forming eye and strike the dense vapor knot after the dart. Affinity signal: Affinity counterplay branches: T1 the vapor half-face exposes its plume-clamp fault after the brief load; T2 the torso cuff exposes its crystal key after transfer; T3 wind arms and orbiting rings expose the weighted load gap after release; T4 crown script exposes the fractured anchor glyph after commitment; T5 vortex, throne, and lamps expose the throne brace when its load releases.
identityInvariants: A hovering humanoid upper body tapers into smoke instead of legs; solidity and scale change only at explicit tiers.
Sapphire or violet smoke, warm inner light, gold, brass, turquoise, silk, and gemstones remain distinct source materials.
Cuffs, rings, headpieces, lamps, and script mark proposed binding status without establishing universal culture or morality.
The body becomes less solid and more spatially dominant from half-face vapor to a palace-scale throne vortex.
telegraph: A faint warm point gathers beneath one unfinished eye while the opposite face remains smoke.
